assay: In vivo cranial-window two-photon imaging of spine and axonal bouton turnover in barrel cortex pyramidal neurons during chronic oral dosing, plus novel object recognition (mouse)
effect_detail: Chronic oral 7,8-DHF increased the GAIN (addition) rates of dendritic spines and of axonal boutons in barrel-cortex pyramidal neurons measured in real time, and improved object recognition memory in the same animals; TrkB expression in the imaged neurons was confirmed first.
quote: DHF increased the gain rates of spines and axonal boutons, as well as improved object recognition memory
caveat: RODENT ONLY. One of the very few rows pairing a structural-plasticity readout with a cognitive readout IN THE SAME ANIMALS, which is why it is here - but the cognitive endpoint is novel object recognition, which is exploration-based and confounded by locomotion/novelty-seeking, and no washout (post-treatment) test is reported, so it is an ON-DRUG effect, not a durable window. Separately, 7,8-DHF's status as a direct TrkB agonist is contested in the literature; the caveat for the DTI head is that its target assignment here may itself be wrong.

assay: 3D automated spine-subtype quantification in AAV-labelled CaMKIIa+ frontal cortex pyramidal neurons after a single dose, in 5-HT2AR-/- vs wild-type mice; plus cued fear extinction
effect_detail: A single DOI dose selectively increased stubby and dynamic thin spines but NOT mature mushroom spines in frontal cortex, and accelerated fear extinction; both effects were absent in 5-HT2AR-/- mice. Chromatin/enhancer changes at synaptic-assembly genes persisted for days after the single exposure.
citation_short: de la Fuente Revenga 2021 Cell Rep
quote: single administration of the psychedelic DOI produces fast-acting effects on frontal cortex dendritic spine structure and acceleration of fear extinction
caveat: RODENT ONLY. The spine-SUBTYPE decomposition is the point: the increase is in immature/labile (stubby, thin) spines, not mushroom spines - so 'increases spine density' and 'increases persistent synapses' are different claims, and a compound-level plasticity score collapsing them is measuring the wrong thing. Same paper reports recognition memory and sensorimotor gating UNCHANGED, i.e. structural plasticity without a cognitive gain - a direct counterexample to the pipeline's implicit spine-to-cognition inference. DOI is a research chemical with no clinical path.

assay: Same cultured rat cortical neuron neuritogenesis/spinogenesis screen as the LSD/DMT/DOI panel (Ly 2018 head-to-head)
effect_detail: Ibogaine was the one compound in the psychedelic panel with no measurable effect on structural plasticity, despite the anti-addictive phenotype the screen was designed to explain. Its metabolite noribogaine WAS active (dendritic arbor complexity, EC50 comparable to ketamine), and ketanserin blocked noribogaine's effect - the authors conclude noribogaine may be the active species in vivo.
quote: was the only psychedelic tested that had absolutely no effect
caveat: RODENT ONLY, in vitro. This is a NEGATIVE inside a positive paper - it never reaches an abstract and will be missing from any ledger built by abstract-scraping, which is a live contamination risk for the pipeline. It also breaks the parent-compound assumption: a compound-level plasticity label for 'ibogaine' is WRONG in direction (parent inert, metabolite active). Any DTI or repurposing head that scores ibogaine from ibogaine's own structure is scoring the wrong molecule. The finding is single-lab, single-assay, no independent replication found.

assay: Two-photon imaging of apical-tuft spine density on layer V mPFC pyramidal neurons, 24 h after a single systemic dose (rat)
effect_detail: Single ketamine dose (10 mg/kg) increased spine density in distal and proximal apical-tuft segments of layer V mPFC neurons 24 h post-injection, plus increased mushroom-spine population and 5-HT/hypocretin-induced EPSC frequency; fully blocked by ICV rapamycin (0.2 nmol). Full text reports n=4-6 animals, ANOVA, *P<0.05 / **P<0.01.
quote: increased synaptic signaling proteins and increased number and function of new spine synapses in the prefrontal cortex of rats
caveat: RODENT ONLY. Abstract carries no effect size; the numbers above come from the PMC figure legends (PMC3116441), not from a reported CI. This is the founding citation for 'ketamine = psychoplastogen', but Zhornitsky 2023 (PMID 37435405) reviewed 84 studies and found MIXED spine/synaptic-marker results for single-dose ketamine under BASAL (non-stressed) conditions - i.e. exactly the healthy-adult condition G1 cares about. Treating this row as a healthy-organism window-opening effect over-reads it.

assay: Chronic longitudinal two-photon imaging of mPFC spine formation/elimination with optogenetic ablation of newly formed spines (mouse, corticosterone stress model)
effect_detail: Antidepressant-dose ketamine selectively rescued spines that stress had eliminated and restored coordinated multicellular ensemble activity; targeted ablation of the ketamine-induced new spines abolished the MAINTENANCE of the behavioural effect at 2-7 days but left its INDUCTION intact.
quote: Prefrontal spinogenesis was required for the long-term maintenance of antidepressant effects on motivated escape behavior but not for their initial induction
caveat: RODENT ONLY, and a stress/depression model - NOT a healthy adult, so it does not touch the G1 zero-row ledger. The dissociation is the load-bearing part: structural plasticity was necessary for DURABILITY but not for the acute effect. Any pipeline that scores a compound as window-opening from an ACUTE readout is scoring the wrong half of this mechanism. Effect sizes are in figures, not the abstract.

assay: Dendritic arbor complexity (Sholl) and spinogenesis in cultured rat cortical neurons, plus in vivo spine/synapse measures; ketanserin-blockable, TrkB/mTOR/5-HT2A dependent
effect_detail: LSD, DMT and DOI each robustly increased neuritogenesis and/or spinogenesis in vitro and in vivo with increased synapse number and function (fluorescence microscopy + electrophysiology); effects blocked by ketanserin and by TrkB/mTOR pathway inhibition. Noribogaine increased dendritic arbor complexity with an EC50 comparable to ketamine.
quote: serotonergic psychedelics are capable of robustly increasing neuritogenesis and/or spinogenesis both in vitro and in vivo
caveat: RODENT ONLY, and the bulk of the compound panel is CULTURED NEURONS at ~10 uM - concentrations with no defensible relationship to human exposure. Abstract reports no effect sizes. Structural plasticity in a dish is the weakest possible evidence for a cognitive window and should be down-weighted relative to the in vivo OD and behavioural rows; using it to label LSD/DMT/DOI as window-openers at compound level imports the in vitro artefact risk wholesale.

assay: Chronic two-photon imaging of apical dendritic spines of layer 5 pyramidal neurons in mouse medial frontal cortex, single dose, followed to 1 month
effect_detail: Single dose produced ~10% increases in BOTH spine size and spine density, driven by an elevated spine formation rate; change present within 24 h and still present 1 month later. Also ameliorated a stress-related behavioural deficit and elevated excitatory neurotransmission.
quote: a single dose of psilocybin led to ~10% increases in spine size and density, driven by an elevated spine formation rate
caveat: RODENT ONLY. The ~10% is the strongest durability evidence in the lane (1 month, structural) but it is STRUCTURE, not cognition - no cognitive-gain endpoint was measured, so it cannot be promoted into the G1 durable-gain ledger. Note the direction of inference the pipeline must not make: persistent spines in mouse mPFC is not evidence of a persistent human cognitive window, and there is no human assay that could test it (see G4).

assay: Whole-cell patch clamp + two-photon image analysis of spine synapse number and function on layer V PFC pyramidal neurons after a single low dose (rat)
effect_detail: A single low dose rapidly increased mTORC1 signalling (phospho-mTORC1 pathway proteins) and the number and function of spine synapses on layer V PFC pyramidal neurons; the behavioural (forced swim) effect was blocked by an mTORC1 inhibitor and by an AMPA receptor antagonist.
quote: a single, low dose of scopolamine rapidly increases mTORC1 signaling and the number and function of spine synapses in layer V pyramidal neurons
caveat: RODENT ONLY, no effect sizes in the abstract. Critical asymmetry for this project: scopolamine is the canonical AMNESTIC in human cognition studies - it reliably IMPAIRS episodic memory in healthy adults - while here it increases spine synapses. So the same compound scores window-opening on a structural assay and cognition-impairing on a human behavioural assay. That is a G3-class sign flip across assay families, from a different direction than the donepezil case, and it means structural-plasticity evidence cannot be used as a directional prior for cognitive enhancement.

assay: Dendritic spine density in DIV20 rat cortical cultures plus transcranial two-photon imaging of spine formation/elimination in mouse primary sensory cortex, 24 h after a single dose
effect_detail: TBG increased dendritic spine density in mature (DIV20) cortical cultures to an extent comparable to ibogaine, and in vivo both TBG and DOI increased the spine FORMATION rate with no effect on spine elimination 24 h after a single dose; dendritic growth was blocked by the 5-HT2A antagonist ketanserin.
quote: tabernanthalog was found to promote structural neural plasticity, reduce alcohol- and heroin-seeking behaviour, and produce antidepressant-like effects
caveat: RODENT ONLY. Exact n and p values are deferred to Source Data/Supplementary Table 1 in the paper, so no statistic is quotable from the text itself. Direct internal conflict with the ibogaine row above: here TBG's spine effect is benchmarked AS COMPARABLE TO IBOGAINE in culture, while Ly 2018 scored ibogaine as having no effect in the same class of assay - so the two UC Davis papers do not agree on the ibogaine reference point. Also: the senior author co-founded a company developing these compounds (declared), and TBG is a novel chemical entity with no human data at all.

assay: Extinction of cued fear conditioning in adult mice after chondroitinase-ABC digestion of PNNs in the basolateral amygdala; erasure vs suppression tested by reinstatement/spontaneous recovery
effect_detail: PNN formation in amygdala coincided with the developmental switch from erasable to permanent fear memory. In adults, chABC digestion of PNNs rendered fear memories acquired AFTER treatment susceptible to erasure by extinction (no spontaneous recovery/reinstatement), reproducing the juvenile phenotype.
quote: In adults, degradation of PNNs by chondroitinase ABC specifically rendered subsequently acquired fear memories susceptible to erasure
caveat: RODENT ONLY. Note the temporal restriction that is usually dropped in citation: only memories acquired AFTER PNN removal became erasable - already-consolidated memories were not. A compound-level 'opens a plasticity window' label loses this, and the distinction is the whole clinical proposition. Also a bacterial enzyme (same G2 unrepresentability as the row above), and the readout is a fear/emotional memory window with no cognitive-performance component, so it is orthogonal to healthy-adult cognitive enhancement despite scoring 'opens'.

assay: adult mouse V1 ocular dominance plasticity by intrinsic signal optical imaging and electrophysiology; plus visual acuity recovery with reverse suturing in adult amblyopic mice
effect_detail: 10 mg/kg baicalin (a flavonoid from Scutellaria baicalensis) reactivated adult ocular dominance plasticity; 5 mg/kg and whole Scutellaria water extract did NOT. Baicalin plus reverse suturing restored both OD distribution and visual acuity to normal in adult amblyopic mice. It reduced GAD65/67 and perineuronal nets in V1, and the GABA-A agonist muscimol given during baicalin treatment BLOCKED the rescued plasticity.
citation_short: Neuroimage 2026;: 'Baicalin reactivates ocular dominance plasticity to restore vision from amblyopia in adult mice'
quote: 10 mg/kg baicalin treatment reactivates ODP in adult mice, whereas 5mg/kg or Scutellaria water extract fails to do so
caveat: SINGLE 2026 PAPER, NOT INDEPENDENTLY REPLICATED. Sharp dose discontinuity (10 mg/kg works, 5 mg/kg does not) with no intermediate doses reported is a fragility signal. Abstract-level only — full text not open-access, so I did not retrieve numeric ODI values. Treat as a candidate, not evidence.

assay: adult rat V1 single-unit ocular dominance shift after MD, following intracortical CSPG/perineuronal-net degradation
effect_detail: In adult rats past the critical period MD normally produces no OD shift; after chondroitinase-ABC degradation of chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans, MD produced an OD shift toward the non-deprived eye. PNN assembly was shown to coincide with critical period closure and to be delayed by dark rearing. Numeric OD/CBI values are in the paywalled full text, not the abstract.
quote: After CSPG degradation with chondroitinase-ABC in adult rats, monocular deprivation caused an ocular dominance shift toward the nondeprived eye.
caveat: G2-CRITICAL: the agent is a bacterial ENZYME acting on an extracellular matrix substrate. There is no protein pocket and no pKd — a BindingDB-affinity DTI head cannot represent this lever at all. No human equivalent exists.

assay: adult rat recovery from early MD: ocular dominance, behavioural visual acuity and dendritic spine density after chABC + reverse lid-suture
effect_detail: Chondroitinase ABC combined with reverse lid-suturing in adult rats produced complete recovery of ocular dominance, visual acuity AND dendritic spine density after a critical-period MD. Note the design: the enzyme alone is not the treatment — it is enzyme PLUS forced visual experience, i.e. a drug x training design. Numeric values are in the full text, not the abstract.
quote: chondroitinase ABC treatment coupled with reverse lid-suturing causes a complete recovery of ocular dominance, visual acuity, and dendritic spine density
caveat: The recovery requires coupled reverse-suture training; the compound alone was not sufficient. This is the rodent archetype of the drug x training hypothesis whose human pre-registered test failed in your ledger.

assay: adult human amblyopia: citalopram 20 mg/day + part-time fellow-eye patching vs placebo + patching, two 2-week blocks, randomized double-blind crossover with 2-week washout; amblyopic-eye visual acuity primary, stereoacuity and ERG/VEP secondary
effect_detail: No statistically significant difference in amblyopic-eye acuity change between active (mean +/- SD = 0.08 +/- 0.16 logMAR) and placebo (mean = -0.01 +/- 0.03 logMAR) blocks; note the active-arm mean is POSITIVE logMAR, i.e. worse. No treatment effects on any secondary outcome including electrophysiological measures. 3 of 7 participants improved >=0.1 logMAR in the active but not the placebo block. Preregistered ACTRN12611000669998.
citation_short: Lagas, Black, Thompson et al., Neural Plast 2019;2019:5857243
quote: There were no statistically significant differences in amblyopic eye visual acuity change between the active
caveat: SEVERELY UNDERPOWERED AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO: 7 randomized against a prespecified 20 (65% under-enrolment). The '3 of 7 responders' framing is a post-hoc subgroup with no placebo-arm denominator control — do NOT let it enter the corpus as a positive. Patients, not healthy adults.

assay: adult rat V1 rapid ocular dominance shift after brief (<=3 d) MD preceded by complete visual deprivation (dark exposure)
effect_detail: Brief MD is ineffective in adults; preceded by dark exposure it produced a persistent juvenile-like OD shift driven by rapid depression of the deprived-eye response plus potentiation of the non-deprived-eye response. Accompanied by a decrease in GABA-A relative to AMPA receptors and a return to the juvenile NMDA receptor form. Effect persisted for days even if binocular vision intervened before MD.
quote: juvenile-like ocular dominance plasticity can be reactivated in adult rodent visual cortex when monocular deprivation is preceded by visual deprivation
caveat: THE CAUSAL LABEL IS WRONG — the same group later showed it is LIGHT REINTRODUCTION, not darkness, that reactivates plasticity (PMID 28875930). Any corpus row encoding 'dark exposure' as the causal agent has the wrong causal variable.

assay: mouse V1 ocular dominance plasticity after MD; benzodiazepine enhancement of GABA transmission in GAD65 knockouts and in immature wild-type mice
effect_detail: Benzodiazepines applied to GAD65-null mice of any age, and to immature wild-type mice before their natural critical period, UNMASKED ocular dominance plasticity (precocious OPENING). But chronic early diazepam rendered the same mutant animals INSENSITIVE to monocular deprivation as adults (permanent CLOSING), matching normal wild-type adults. The authors frame this as an inhibitory threshold that triggers the critical period once in life.
quote: Enhancing GABA-mediated transmission early in life rendered mutant animals insensitive to monocular deprivation as adults
caveat: DIRECTION IS GENUINELY NOT A SCALAR for this compound: same drug, same assay, opposite sign depending on developmental timing. A compound-level window score cannot encode this. Separately, cortical diazepam BLOCKS the fluoxetine effect in adults (PMID 18420937), which is the adult-onset 'closes' reading.

assay: healthy adult human perceptual eye dominance shift after 2 h monocular patching, measured by binocular phase combination; donepezil 5 mg oral vs lactose placebo, double-blind crossover
effect_detail: n = 12 healthy adults, within-subject crossover. BOTH conditions showed a significant post-patching shift favouring the patched eye, but donepezil significantly REDUCED its magnitude and duration: post-hoc paired t-test on the main effect of session t(11) = -4.9, p < 0.001, M = -1.27, 95% CI [-1.79, -0.75]; ANOVA session effect Wilks' lambda = 0.5, F(1,11) = 11.1, p < 0.01, partial eta-squared = 0.50; interaction F(4,44) = 0.83, p > 0.05. Under placebo the shift stayed significant through 60 min; under donepezil it was significant only at the first post-patch timepoint.
citation_short: Sheynin, Chamoun, Baldwin, Rosa-Neto, Hess, Vaucher, Front Neurosci 2019;13:22
quote: treated with donepezil was significantly reduced relative to the placebo control condition
caveat: THE G3 ANCHOR, AND IT HOLDS. Same drug INCREASES human perceptual learning (PMID 20850321). n = 12, single 5 mg dose, acute readout only (<=60 min) — this is not a durable window measurement and says nothing about post-washout gain.

assay: healthy adult human binocular rivalry dynamics (perceptual suppression depth, interocular competition rate, mixed/superimposition percepts); donepezil 5 mg oral vs placebo, crossover
effect_detail: n = 23 (13 male), two crossover sessions, rivalry measured before and after donepezil 5 mg or lactose placebo. Donepezil attenuated perceptual suppression during binocular rivalry, reduced the overall rate of interocular competition, and increased the visibility of superimposition mixed percepts. The authors interpret this as cholinergic activity counteracting GABAergic inhibitory drive in visual cortex.
citation_short: Sheynin, Proulx, Hess et al., J Neurosci 2020;40(27):5208-5213
quote: enhanced cholinergic potentiation attenuates perceptual suppression during binocular rivalry, reducing the overall rate of interocular competition
caveat: Coded MIXED deliberately. The MECHANISTIC direction is plasticity-permissive (reduced cortical inhibition, the canonical window-opening signature), yet the same drug in the same lab REDUCES the actual MD-induced OD shift (PMID 30766471). A mechanism-level proxy and a behaviour-level window measure disagree for one drug — a direct warning against scoring windows from mechanism.

assay: adult rat V1 ocular dominance shift after monocular deprivation (VEP C/I ratio + single-unit), plus visual acuity recovery in adult amblyopic rats
effect_detail: Chronic fluoxetine in adult rats reinstated an MD-induced ocular dominance shift and restored visual acuity in long-term-deprived amblyopic adults; accompanied by reduced intracortical inhibition and increased BDNF. Cortical diazepam infusion abolished the effect. NO numeric effect size appears in the abstract and the Science full text is paywalled and was not retrieved — I am deliberately NOT quoting a numeric C/I VEP ratio for this row because I could not verify one against the source.
quote: reinstates ocular dominance plasticity in adulthood and promotes the recovery of visual functions in adult amblyopic animals
caveat: Effect size unverified at source (paywalled). Rodent only. Human replication on an OD-type readout has since FAILED (PMID 30150750, PMID 27807412) — this is the single most-cited row in the field and it does not translate.

assay: adult human amblyopia: Phase 2 randomized double-blind multicenter trial, fluoxetine 20 mg vs placebo for 10 weeks, with daily computerized perceptual training and eye patching in BOTH arms; amblyopic-eye visual acuity primary
effect_detail: n = 42 (fluoxetine 22, placebo 20). Mean treatment-group difference in acuity improvement 0.027 logMAR, 95% CI -0.057 to 0.110, p = 0.524. BOTH arms improved substantially from baseline: fluoxetine -0.167 logMAR (95% CI -0.226 to -0.108, p < 0.001) and placebo -0.194 logMAR (95% CI -0.254 to -0.133, p < 0.001) — the placebo arm numerically improved MORE.
citation_short: Huttunen, Castrén, Thompson et al., Sci Rep 2018;8(1):12830
quote: the mean treatment group difference in visual acuity improvement was only 0.027 logMAR units
caveat: THE CLEANEST FAILED TRANSLATION IN THE LANE: the rodent headline (PMID 18420937) tested directly in humans with adequate n and a drug x training design, and the drug contributes nothing while the TRAINING produces a large real effect in both arms. This is the exact failure mode of your pre-registered drug x training test. Patients, not healthy adults.

assay: adult mouse V1 ocular dominance plasticity reactivated by light reintroduction after dark exposure; MMP-9 pharmacological inhibition, Mmp9-/- knockout, and hyaluronidase rescue
effect_detail: Light reintroduction after dark exposure — not the dark exposure itself — triggers perisynaptic MMP-9 activation enriched at thalamocortical synapses, which degrades the ECM and reactivates adult OD plasticity. Reactivation is BLOCKED by MMP-9 pharmacological inhibition and ABSENT in Mmp9-/- mice, and is RESCUED in those mice by hyaluronidase, an independent ECM-degrading enzyme. This is a necessity + sufficiency pair on the ECM node.
citation_short: Murase, Winsor, Quinlan et al., eLife 2017;6:e27345
quote: is absent in Mmp9-/- mice, and is rescued by hyaluronidase, an enzyme that degrades core ECM components
caveat: G2-CRITICAL: both the opener (hyaluronidase) and the closer (MMP-9 inhibition) act on ECM substrate, not on a druggable binding pocket with a pKd. This row and the two chABC rows together are the measured reason the DTI head cannot see the plasticity levers.

assay: adult mouse V1 ocular dominance index (intrinsic signal imaging) after 4 d MD, plus visual-water-task deprived-eye acuity recovery from amblyopia
effect_detail: Single-dose subanesthetic ketamine reactivated adult OD plasticity: ODI reduced in ketamine vs saline adults, Mann-Whitney U p = 0.0078 (n = 18 ketamine vs n = 16 saline). Deprived-eye perceptual acuity threshold 0.42 cpd with ketamine vs 0.34 cpd control, Mann-Whitney U p = 0.0008 (n = 12 vs n = 11), with no significant change in the non-deprived eye (p = 0.1927). Mechanism: downregulation of NRG1 in PV interneurons producing sustained cortical disinhibition; blocked by exogenous NRG1 and by PV-targeted receptor knockout.
citation_short: Grieco, Qiao, Xu et al., Curr Biol 2020;30(18):3591-3603.e8
quote: single-dose ketamine reactivates adult mouse visual cortical plasticity and promotes functional recovery of visual acuity defects from amblyopia
caveat: Nonparametric tests on modest n. Mechanism is PV-interneuron disinhibition via NRG1 — again an E/I-balance node, not an affinity event the DTI head can score. Relevant to G4: human SV2A PET sees nothing 24h post-ketamine, so this rodent window has no human readout.

assay: Ocular-dominance shift after 7-day monocular deprivation in adult mice (3 injections), with WFA quantification of PNNs around PV+ interneurons in the same animals
effect_detail: Ketamine (3 or 20 mg/kg) and R,R-HNK both facilitated the OD shift in monocularly deprived adult mice; R,R-HNK showed the larger effect size. PNN levels around PV+ interneurons were UNCHANGED by either drug. In vitro, both disrupted the TRKB-PTPsigma interaction.
quote: Treatment with ketamine or R,R-HNK failed to influence the levels of perineuronal nets (PNNs) surrounding parvalbumin-positive interneurons
caveat: THE MOST IMPORTANT ROW IN THIS LANE FOR G3. It is the only paper I found measuring a functional window assay and the PNN substrate in the same animals, and the two DISSOCIATE: window opens, PNN does not move. This falsifies the assumption that a PNN/ECM readout can proxy a window label, and it means a compound-level 'opens window' score built from PNN evidence and one built from OD evidence are not the same quantity. RODENT ONLY. Abstract reports no numeric effect sizes or CIs; 'higher effect size' is the authors' wording, not a statistic I can quote.

assay: residual amblyopia in children aged 7-12: 16 weeks oral levodopa (with carbidopa) three times daily vs placebo, both arms patching the fellow eye 2 h/day; mean change in best-corrected amblyopic-eye visual acuity at 18 weeks
effect_detail: n = 139 children, randomized placebo-controlled. Amblyopic-eye acuity improved 5.2 letters with levodopa vs 3.8 letters with placebo; difference adjusted for baseline acuity +1.4 letters, 1-sided p = 0.06, 2-sided 95% CI -0.4 to 3.3 letters. No serious adverse effects during treatment.
citation_short: PEDIG (Pediatric Eye Disease Investigator Group), Ophthalmology 2015;122(5):874-81
quote: oral levodopa while continuing to patch 2 hours daily does not produce a clinically or statistically meaningful improvement
caveat: BEST-POWERED HUMAN TRIAL IN THE LANE (n = 139) AND IT IS NULL. Population is CHILDREN 7-12 with residual amblyopia, so it is neither healthy nor adult — if anything the window should be MORE open here, making the null stronger against levodopa. Note the CI crosses zero while the 1-sided p is 0.06: an exact borderline case for a promote-criterion.

assay: Reactivation of ocular-dominance plasticity in ADULT mouse V1 by light reintroduction after dark exposure, with intracortical MMP-9 inhibitor infusion and Mmp9-/- comparison
effect_detail: Light reintroduction after dark exposure triggered ECM degradation and reactivated plasticity in adult V1; MMP-9 Inhibitor I (CAS 1177749-58-4, IC50 = 5 nM) infused intracortically at 5 nM via osmotic minipump for 6 days prevented the ECM degradation, and reactivation was absent in Mmp9-/- mice. Plasticity was rescued by hyaluronidase.
quote: LRx triggers degradation of the ECM, which is blocked by pharmacological inhibition or genetic ablation of matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9)
caveat: RODENT ONLY, and the only CLOSES_WINDOW row in this lane - it is a loss-of-function control inside a positive paper, not a study designed to find window closure, so it is not evidence about base rates of closure. Directly relevant to G2: MMP9 is one of the targets where the BindingDB pKd head measures AUROC 0.42 with permutation p>0.7, and all MMP9 evidence available here is INHIBITION; I found NO compound that pharmacologically increases MMP9 activity, so the 'MMP9 modulator' lever the pipeline wants to score has no positive-direction ligand to score. Pharmacological convergence with the Mmp9-/- genetic result is the main strength. Compare Spolidoro 2012 (PMID 21685398), where MMP inhibition also prevented the MD-induced spine-density increase - but that paper's specific inhibitor is not named in the retrievable text, so do not assign it a compound identity.

assay: adult mouse V1 contralateral bias index after MD in Lynx1 knockouts; and visual acuity recovery in adult wild-type mice given a cholinesterase inhibitor plus deprived-eye reopening
effect_detail: Lynx1 protein rises with age and prevents adult V1 plasticity by braking nicotinic ACh receptor signalling; removing it restores adult OD plasticity (adult MD shifted the OD distribution of Lynx1 KO mice, CBI = 0.55, 216 cells, 8 mice). In wild-type adults, reopening the deprived eye together with a cholinesterase inhibitor restored vision: AChEI group 0.48 +/- 0.06 cyc/deg, 4 mice, P < 0.05 vs eye-opening alone.
quote: we identified an increase in expression of Lynx1 protein in mice that prevented plasticity in the primary visual cortex late in life
caveat: G3 HEADLINE ROW. A cholinesterase inhibitor OPENS the rodent OD window here, while donepezil — the same drug class — CLOSES the human OD shift (PMID 30766471). n = 4 mice in the AChEI acuity arm. The rodent agent is physostigmine, not donepezil; no primary rodent donepezil-on-OD study was found.

assay: Ocular-dominance plasticity in ADULT mice after pharmacological stimulation of histone acetylation, with ERK/MSK/H3-H4 acetylation and CREB-mediated transcription measured in vivo
effect_detail: In juveniles, visual stimulation drove ERK-dependent MSK and histone H3 phosphorylation and H3-H4 acetylation alongside CREB-mediated transcription; in adults ERK and MSK were still inducible but CREB-mediated expression and H3-H4 modification were weak. Trichostatin treatment of adults restored histone acetylation and promoted ocular-dominance plasticity.
quote: Stimulation of histone acetylation in adult animals by means of trichostatin promoted ocular dominance plasticity
caveat: RODENT ONLY, no effect sizes in the abstract, and this paper carries a published erratum (Neuron 2007;54(1):177) - check which figure it affects before using any number from it. Trichostatin A is a research-tool HDAC inhibitor with no plausible repurposing path (toxicity, no oral exposure), so it is mechanistically informative but useless as a candidate. Mechanistically it is the same pan-HDAC lever as the valproate rows, so these three HDAC rows are NOT three independent lines of evidence and must not be counted as such in any aggregation.

assay: Recovery of visual acuity (VEP electrophysiology + behavioural visual water task) in adult rats long-term monocularly deprived from the critical period, chronic i.p. HDAC inhibitor + reverse lid suture
effect_detail: Chronic i.p. valproic acid or sodium butyrate, each combined with reverse lid-suturing, produced complete recovery of visual acuity in long-term monocularly deprived adult rats, confirmed both electrophysiologically and behaviourally; neither was tested without the reverse-suture experience.
quote: caused a complete recovery of visual acuity, tested electrophysiologically and behaviorally
caveat: RODENT ONLY, no effect sizes in the abstract. The load-bearing caveat: the drug alone did nothing measurable - recovery required DRUG + FORCED EXPERIENCE (reverse lid suture). That is the drug x training interaction hypothesis, and the pipeline's pre-registered human test of exactly that hypothesis FAILED with the contrast reversing sign once n>=25 was enforced (G1). So this row should be read as prior-consistent rodent evidence for a hypothesis that has already been falsified once in humans, not as support for it. Two HDAC inhibitors is convergent chemistry but both are pan-HDAC and pleiotropic.

assay: TMS battery in healthy adults: paired-pulse intracortical inhibition and facilitation, cortical silent period, stimulus-response curves, M responses and F waves, plus reaction time, nine-hole-peg and d2 attention tests; 200 mg single oral dose vs placebo
effect_detail: n=10 healthy volunteers, randomised double-blind crossover, tested pre-dose and at 3 h and 24 h. Modafinil did not change intracortical excitatory or inhibitory properties, corticospinal excitability, or alpha-motoneuronal excitability. Nine-hole-peg and d2 attention performance improved equally in modafinil and placebo arms (practice effect). No significant modafinil-vs-placebo difference on any measure.
citation_short: Liepert et al., J Neural Transm 2004
quote: Modafinil did not change excitatory or inhibitory properties in the motor cortex
caveat: Assay family is 'other', NOT tms_ltp: this study measured resting excitability (SICI/ICF, silent period, S-R curve), it did NOT apply any plasticity-induction protocol (no PAS, tDCS or TBS), so it cannot speak to LTP-like plasticity - it only shows modafinil does not shift the baseline against which plasticity would be measured. n=10, single dose, absence of evidence at this power is weak. NOT FOUND: no modafinil x PAS/tDCS/TBS study and no modafinil x human perceptual-learning study exist in this lane.

assay: Social reward learning (conditioned place preference) critical-period reopening in adult mice, with RNA-seq of open- vs closed-state differentially expressed genes
effect_detail: Psilocybin pretreatment produced a significant mean shift into the open state (P = 1.12 x 10^-6) versus saline (P = 0.72); LSD (i.p. 1 ug/kg) likewise reopened the critical period (P = 1.76 x 10^-9) versus saline (P = 0.90). Reopening duration was proportional to human acute subjective-effect duration; ECM reorganisation was the shared downstream transcriptomic signature.
quote: reorganization of the extracellular matrix is a common downstream mechanism underlying psychedelic drug-mediated critical period reopening
caveat: RODENT ONLY. This is the paper most often cited as proof that psychedelics reopen critical periods generally, but the assay is a SOCIAL REWARD window with no cognitive-performance readout, and the ECM claim is TRANSCRIPTOMIC (differentially expressed genes), not a direct PNN measurement - which is exactly where it conflicts with Cannarozzo 2023's direct PNN null. Both cannot be casually folded into one compound-level score. The 'proportional to subjective-effect duration' claim is a cross-species correlation over a handful of drugs, not a tested dose-response.

assay: motion direction discrimination, 5-day training course, double-blind placebo-controlled within-subject crossover, 5 mg oral before each session
effect_detail: n=12 healthy adults. Improvement in motion direction discrimination threshold 6.2 +/- 2.1 deg under donepezil vs 2.2 +/- 0.8 deg under placebo; between-condition t36=3.1, p<0.05. Direction selectivity of learning 4.0 +/- 1.2 deg (t36=3.94, p<0.05) vs placebo 1.4 +/- 1.1 deg (t36=1.34, n.s.), difference t36=2.82, p<0.05. Location selectivity 3.0 +/- 1.2 deg (t36=2.36, p<0.05) vs placebo -1.2 +/- 1.0 deg (n.s.), difference t36=2.68, p<0.05. Learning rate also faster under donepezil (permutation test p<0.05).
quote: cholinergic enhancement augmented perceptual learning for stimuli having the same direction of motion and visual field location used during training
caveat: n=12, single lab, drug present during every training session so this is drug-gated encoding, not a drug-free window. Learning gain is stimulus-specific (donepezil INCREASED specificity, i.e. reduced transfer), so it is not general cognitive enhancement. Same cohort feeds the 2013 follow-up (PMID 23755006), which is therefore not independent.

assay: motion direction discrimination, long-term follow-up retest 5-15 months after end of training, no drug administered at follow-up
effect_detail: 8 of the original 12 subjects retested 5-15 months post-training, drug-free. Percent learning retained: donepezil-trained condition 47.1 +/- 4.6% vs placebo-trained condition 34.2 +/- 6.9%; effect of training condition F(2,12)=6.0, p=0.016; direct comparison signed-rank p=0.036; 7 of 8 participants showed more retained learning in the donepezil-trained condition. Threshold in the donepezil condition essentially unchanged from post-training (7.4 +/- 1.1 deg) to follow-up (7.4 +/- 0.7 deg), i.e. no decay.
quote: Increases in performance associated with training under donepezil were evident in follow-up retesting, indicating that cholinergic enhancement has beneficial long-term effects
caveat: THE closest thing in this lane to a durable post-washout gain in healthy adults, and it still fails several G1 bars: n=8, non-independent (subset of PMID 20850321 cohort), single lab, never replicated, no drug-free control training arm at follow-up, retention interval varied 5-15 months per subject. The retained gain is task- and stimulus-specific perceptual learning, not transferable cognition, and the drug acted during training rather than opening a window that persisted.

assay: 3D multiple object tracking (3D-MOT) perceptual-cognitive training, 5 sessions 7 days apart, 5 mg oral 3 h pre-session, parallel-group placebo control
effect_detail: n=17 healthy young adults (donepezil n=9, placebo n=8). Donepezil group reached significant speed-threshold improvement by session 4 (p=0.003, maintained session 5 p=0.001); placebo group only at session 5 (p=0.002). BUT no significant between-group difference at any timepoint (Kruskal-Wallis p>0.05), despite 20-50% larger percent change from baseline in the donepezil group after week 3. Long-lasting subgroup retest at 4-14 months in n=9 suggested persistence. No effect on basic motion/orientation discrimination (n=10, uncontrolled pre-post).
citation_short: Chamoun et al., Front Hum Neurosci 2017
quote: there were no significant drug effects on the performance levels compared to placebo
caveat: The only independent-lab donepezil perceptual-training attempt found, and its between-group test is NULL. The positive claim rests on within-group timing of significance onset, which is a classic difference-in-significance fallacy. Parallel-group design with n=8-9 per arm is badly underpowered. The basic-vision arm had no placebo control. Treat as a partial non-replication of PMID 20850321, not a confirmation.

assay: motion direction discrimination (MDD) perceptual learning over 5 days plus TMS cortical excitability (phosphene and motor thresholds); 19-day 20 mg/day fluoxetine vs placebo, double-blind parallel groups
effect_detail: n=20 healthy adults (fluoxetine n=10, placebo n=10). Both groups learned (session effect F3,47=11.4, p<0.001) but session x treatment interaction F3,47=0.51, p=0.7; learning slopes 1.7 +/- 1.2 (active) vs 1.8 +/- 2.4 (placebo), t18=0.1, p=0.9. Full transfer to untrained stimulus in BOTH groups, no group difference. Phosphene thresholds: session x group F4,43=2.0, p=0.11 (n.s.). Resting motor thresholds stable, F6,108=0.72, p=0.6. Separately, a single dose of triazolam (GABA-A positive modulator) selectively impaired UNTRAINED-stimulus performance without affecting trained performance.
citation_short: Lagas et al., Front Hum Neurosci 2016
quote: Fluoxetine did not enhance the magnitude or rate of perceptual learning
caveat: Rare and valuable: the SAME subjects were tested on a perceptual-learning assay and on TMS excitability, and both were null - so this null is not an assay-selection artifact. Direct translational failure of the rat fluoxetine/visual-cortex-plasticity result. Caveats: n=10 per arm, parallel groups, phosphene subgroup only n=13 total (8 placebo vs 5 active), and TMS here measured excitability, not an LTP-induction protocol. Fluoxetine is not citalopram, so the SSRI contrast with PMID 19427633 is class-level, not compound-level.

assay: texture discrimination task (TDT), overnight consolidation; nicotine-containing chewing tobacco for 1 h immediately post-training vs matched non-nicotine control substance
effect_detail: Two groups of non-smoking men; nicotine given only during the post-training consolidation window, not during training or retest. Both groups improved in accuracy and speed at next-day retest, with improvements specific to retinal location and texture orientation (implicating early visual cortex). Group comparison showed learning effects were larger in the nicotine group. Concurrent EEG showed reduced alpha activity and shorter P300 latencies under nicotine.
quote: learning effects were more pronounced in the nicotine group than in the control group
caveat: NO numeric test statistic is reported in the abstract and the full text is paywalled - the effect size and p value are UNVERIFIED by me. Parallel-group (not crossover), men only, sample size not stated in the abstract. Route is oral chewing tobacco, so dose and plasma level are uncontrolled. Directionally this row conflicts with PMID 23133419 (nicotine spray abolished facilitatory plasticity), so the nicotine sign is assay- and route-dependent.

assay: Double-blind placebo-controlled absolute-pitch (AP) training in healthy adult men, 2 weeks valproate vs placebo, 18-item pitch identification test; parallel arm then crossover arm
effect_detail: Arm 1 (n=23): VPA 5.09 vs placebo 3.50 correct of 18 (chance = 3); one-way ANOVA effect of Condition F(1,21)=6.37, p=0.02. VPA group above chance t(10)=4.08 p=0.002; placebo at chance t(11)=1.32 p=0.21. No correlation of AP score with blood VPA (r=0.36, n=11, p=0.28) or with training sessions completed (r=0.13, n=23, p=0.55).
quote: adult men who took valproate (VPA) (a HDAC inhibitor) learned to identify pitch significantly better than those taking placebo
caveat: THE ONLY HUMAN ROW IN THIS LANE, and it is far weaker than its citation record implies. The crossover arm did NOT replicate cleanly: significant Condition x Order interaction F(1,15)=8.85 p=0.009, with the effect present only in the VPA-first group F(1,8)=20.25 p=0.002 and ABSENT in the placebo-first group F(1,7)=1.13 p=0.32 - i.e. order-dependent, consistent with carryover or an unblinding/expectancy artefact (VPA has salient side effects). No baseline AP score was obtainable by design. Males only, n=23, single site, p=0.02 in the primary arm. Dose-response is null (no blood-level correlation). Crucially it is a PERCEPTUAL-LEARNING window, not spine or PNN - so it cannot be used to validate any spine/PNN-derived window label, and it is ON-DRUG with no post-washout retest, so it adds nothing to the G1 durable-gain ledger.

assay: Long-term novel object recognition memory and perirhinal cortex LTD after localised PNN digestion in adult mice, benchmarked against Crtl1/Hapln1 knockout
effect_detail: Genetic PNN attenuation (Crtl1 KO) enhanced long-term object recognition memory and facilitated perirhinal LTD; localised chondroitinase-ABC digestion produced an identical prolongation of memory. The chABC memory enhancement ATTENUATED over time, tracking PNN regeneration.
quote: Identical prolongation of memory follows localized digestion of PNNs with chondroitinase ABC
caveat: RODENT ONLY - but the closest thing in this lane to an actual COGNITIVE ENHANCEMENT result from PNN removal, and it explicitly FADES as PNNs regrow. That is the cleanest available statement that the PNN 'window' effect is not durable post-washout, which is the exact quantity G1 finds has zero verified human examples. Convergent genetic + enzymatic evidence is a strength; the object-recognition confounds and the bacterial-enzyme G2 problem remain. No effect sizes in the abstract.

assay: anodal and cathodal tDCS of M1; single 20 mg oral dose of citalopram vs placebo, single-blind randomised crossover, single-pulse TMS MEP readout
effect_detail: n=12 healthy subjects. Under placebo, anodal tDCS enhanced and cathodal tDCS reduced excitability for about 60-120 min. Citalopram enhanced and prolonged anodal-tDCS facilitation and CONVERTED cathodal-tDCS-induced inhibition into facilitation - i.e. it biased plasticity toward facilitation in both directions of induction.
quote: Citalopram enhanced and prolonged the facilitation induced by anodal tDCS, whereas it turned cathodal tDCS-induced inhibition into facilitation
caveat: Directionally consistent (facilitation-biased) within this assay, but the conversion of LTD-like into LTP-like plasticity means the drug is not 'enhancing plasticity' - it is biasing sign, which a window score would misread. n=12, SINGLE-blind (not double), Gottingen lab, single acute dose. Contrast sharply with the fluoxetine double-null on perceptual learning AND excitability (PMID 27807412): the serotonergic 'window' does not survive the change of assay or of compound within class.

assay: facilitatory PAS-25 and excitability-diminishing PAS-10 of left M1; single 20 mg oral citalopram vs placebo, single-blind randomised crossover, MEPs tracked to the next evening
effect_detail: n=14 healthy subjects. After citalopram, inhibitory PAS-induced after-effects were ABOLISHED and excitatory PAS-induced after-effects were enhanced only TRENDWISE (not significant) versus the respective placebo conditions. Authors interpret this as serotonin shifting PAS plasticity toward facilitation.
quote: inhibitory PAS-induced after-effects were abolished and excitatory PAS-induced after-effects were enhanced trendwise
caveat: The facilitatory half of the effect is a NON-SIGNIFICANT trend - the significant result is the removal of inhibitory plasticity. Read strictly, citalopram did not significantly open the focal LTP-like door; it closed the LTD-like one. That is a weaker and differently-signed result than the same lab's tDCS study (PMID 19427633), i.e. citalopram is also assay-dependent. n=14, single-blind, Gottingen, single acute dose, left M1 only.

assay: anodal tDCS of M1, MEP readout to the morning after stimulation; amphetamine vs placebo, with dextromethorphan and propranolol control arms
effect_detail: Amphetamine significantly enhanced and prolonged anodal-tDCS-induced excitability increases: after-effects lasted until the morning after tDCS vs approximately 1 h under placebo. Prolongation was most pronounced for long-term effects; short-term enhancement was only slightly increased. Co-administered dextromethorphan (NMDA antagonist) blocked the enhancement entirely, and propranolol (beta-adrenergic antagonist) shortened the after-effects.
quote: Amphetamine significantly enhanced and prolonged increases in anodal, tDCS-induced, long-lasting excitability
caveat: The dextromethorphan and propranolol arms make the mechanism claim (NMDA-dependent consolidation, adrenergically gated) unusually well supported for this literature. But: no sample size or numeric statistics in the abstract, single lab (Gottingen), only the FACILITATORY protocol is reported here, so within-drug assay-dependence was not tested. NOT FOUND: no human perceptual-learning counterpart for amphetamine, so amphetamine contributes nothing to the cross-family sign-consistency test.

assay: anodal and cathodal tDCS of M1, MEP readout; partial NMDA agonist D-cycloserine vs placebo
effect_detail: D-cycloserine selectively potentiated the DURATION (not the initial magnitude) of anodal-tDCS-induced motor cortical excitability enhancement. Cathodal-tDCS-induced inhibition was unaffected. D-cycloserine alone did not modulate excitability, so the drug consolidated stimulation-induced plasticity rather than inducing it.
quote: D-CYC selectively potentiated the duration of motor cortical excitability enhancements induced by anodal tDCS
caveat: No sample size and no numeric test statistics in the abstract; not independently verified by me beyond the abstract text. Effect is consolidation-of-induced-plasticity, which is the theoretically cleanest 'window' story in the set, but it is single-lab (Gottingen) and has no perceptual-learning counterpart - NOT FOUND: no human perceptual-learning study of d-cycloserine. Selectivity for the facilitatory direction means even this compound does not scale a generic 'window'.

assay: visual sensory tetanisation (EEG visual LTP): high-frequency visual stimulation, change in visual evoked potential N1 and P2; single 0.44 mg/kg IV ketamine vs active placebo (remifentanil 1.7 ng/mL), double-blind crossover
effect_detail: n=30 patients with depression, LTP recorded 3-4 h post-infusion. Visual LTP was demonstrated in both components: N1 p=0.00002, P2 p=2.31 x 10-11. Ketamine specifically enhanced P2 potentiation relative to active placebo, p=0.017. Dynamic causal modelling showed recruitment of forward and intrinsic connections with complementary ketamine effects. 70% of participants had >=50% reduction in MADRS within 1 day.
citation_short: Sumner et al., Biol Psychiatry CNNI 2020
quote: Ketamine specifically enhanced P2 potentiation compared with placebo (p = .017)
caveat: PATIENTS WITH DEPRESSION, not healthy adults - so it does not bear on the healthy-adult ledger, and a baseline-deficit-correction reading is fully available (cf. the doc-291-style 'restores impaired' vs 'enhances normal' distinction). Only 1 of 2 components moved (N1 null, P2 p=0.017, uncorrected for the two components). Single timepoint 3-4 h post-dose, so nothing about durability. Active placebo is remifentanil, an opioid, which is not inert for arousal. NOT FOUND: no equivalent healthy-adult ketamine visual-LTP study.

assay: anodal/cathodal tDCS (non-focal) and PAS-25 (focal) of M1; dopamine precursor levodopa vs placebo in healthy subjects
effect_detail: Levodopa REVERSED the sign of non-focal plasticity - anodal-tDCS excitability enhancement became inhibition - while prolonging cathodal-tDCS inhibition, and it STABILISED the focal PAS-25 excitability increase. All after-effects, regardless of sign, were prolonged by a factor of roughly 20.
quote: administering L-dopa turns the unspecific excitability enhancement caused by anodal tDCS into inhibition
caveat: An outright SIGN REVERSAL in one assay (tDCS) alongside stabilisation in another (PAS), same drug, same study. A compound-level 'opens window' label for levodopa would be flatly wrong. No sample size or numeric statistics in the abstract (single-lab Gottingen, typical n=12). The '20x prolongation' is the headline number but it applies to inhibitory as well as facilitatory after-effects, so it is a duration effect, not a directional enhancement.

assay: anodal and cathodal tDCS of M1 under 25, 100 and 200 mg L-dopa vs placebo; MEP readout; dose-response design
effect_detail: n=12 healthy subjects. Relative to placebo, LOW (25 mg) and HIGH (200 mg) doses abolished both facilitatory and inhibitory plasticity; the MEDIUM (100 mg) dose prolonged inhibitory plasticity and converted facilitatory plasticity into inhibition. Result is an inverted-U, non-linear dose dependence of cortical plasticity on dopamine.
quote: low and high dosages of L-dopa abolished facilitatory as well as inhibitory plasticity
caveat: Independent of the assay-dependence problem, this row shows DOSE alone flips the sign within a single assay in a single cohort. Any compound-level window score must therefore be dose-indexed as well as assay-indexed, and any dose-blind DTI/affinity model is predicting a quantity that does not exist. Caveats: n=12, Gottingen lab, no dose above 200 mg tested, and none of the three doses actually IMPROVED facilitatory plasticity - the 'optimal dose' is inferred, not observed.

assay: PAS-25 (focal facilitatory), PAS-10 (focal inhibitory), anodal and cathodal tDCS of M1; transdermal nicotine patch vs placebo patch in non-smokers; MEP readout to the evening of the following day
effect_detail: n=48 non-smokers (12 per stimulation protocol), placebo-controlled crossover. Nicotine x Stimulation interaction F(3,44)=5.498, p=0.003; Time x Stimulation F(30,440)=3.070, p<0.001; three-way Nicotine x Time x Stimulation F(30,440)=1.848, p=0.005. By protocol: PAS-25 facilitation slightly PROLONGED (significantly larger MEPs at 120 min); PAS-10 inhibition ABOLISHED; anodal-tDCS facilitation ABOLISHED (post-tDCS MEPs not different from baseline); cathodal-tDCS inhibition eliminated, only trendwise vs placebo.
quote: Nicotine abolished or reduced both PAS- and tDCS-induced inhibitory neuroplasticity
caveat: A within-study, within-drug sign flip across assays: focal PAS facilitation preserved/prolonged while non-focal tDCS facilitation was abolished. Directly falsifies a compound-level window label for nicotine. Caveats: n=12 per protocol (between-protocol comparisons are between-subjects), Gottingen lab, left M1 MEP readout only, patch route gives slow sustained levels unlike smoking. Authors frame this as a 'focusing' effect, which is a mechanism claim, not a window claim.

assay: PAS-25, PAS-10, anodal and cathodal tDCS of M1; fast-acting nicotine SPRAY vs placebo in non-smokers
effect_detail: n=48 non-smokers, placebo-controlled. Nicotine spray abolished facilitatory plasticity regardless of whether it was focal (PAS-25) or non-focal (anodal tDCS), abolished PAS-10-induced inhibition, and delayed/weakened cathodal-tDCS excitability reduction.
quote: Nicotine spray abolished facilitatory plasticity irrespective of focality and PAS-10-induced excitability diminution
caveat: CONTRADICTS the same group's own patch study (PMID 21160466), where focal PAS-25 facilitation was preserved/enhanced. Same lab, same protocols, same subject type - only the ROUTE/kinetics differed. This means nicotine's window sign is not even stable within one lab, let alone across assays. It also contradicts PMID 19640784 (nicotine lozenge enhanced iTBS facilitation). No numeric statistics extracted; abstract reports direction only.

assay: intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) of M1, MEPs recorded 40 min post-stimulation; 4 mg nicotine lozenge vs placebo lozenge 60 min pre-iTBS, double-blind crossover
effect_detail: n=10 healthy subjects. Under placebo, iTBS-induced MEP facilitation lasted only ~5 min. Under nicotine, facilitation was more pronounced and still present at 40 min post-iTBS. Control experiment: nicotine alone (no iTBS) had no effect on MEP amplitudes, so the drug did not shift baseline excitability.
quote: These data indicate that the effects of iTBS can be enhanced and prolonged by nicotine
caveat: The only TBS-protocol drug row found for any of the eight target compounds, and the only non-Gottingen nicotine plasticity row (UCL/Rothwell). Its POSITIVE sign for facilitatory plasticity directly opposes PMID 23133419, which abolished facilitatory plasticity with nicotine spray. n=10, 40 min follow-up only (cannot speak to durability), readout is corticospinal MEP amplitude, an indirect LTP proxy. Placebo-arm iTBS effect lasting only 5 min is itself weak, so the interaction rests on an unusually small placebo response.

assay: anodal/cathodal tDCS (non-focal) and PAS-25/PAS-10 (focal, synapse-specific) of M1; cholinesterase inhibitor rivastigmine vs placebo, same healthy subjects
effect_detail: n=12 (tDCS), n=10 (PAS-25), n=10 (PAS-10). Rivastigmine BLOCKED anodal-tDCS excitability enhancement (under placebo the increase stayed significant to 30 min post-tDCS; under drug it was prevented). Cathodal-tDCS inhibition was first reduced then PROLONGED (significant to 2 h vs return to baseline by 60 min under placebo). Facilitatory PAS-25 was ENHANCED and prolonged, drug x PAS interaction F=23.886, p<0.001. Inhibitory PAS-10 was enhanced and prolonged to the same-day evening vs ~30 min under placebo.
quote: Rivastigmine essentially blocked the induction of the global excitability enhancement elicited by anodal tDCS
caveat: THE strongest single piece of evidence for G3 in this lane: the same cholinergic drug, the same subjects, the same session, and the sign of the plasticity effect reverses depending on the induction protocol - so the flip cannot be a cohort, dose, or lab artifact. Compound is rivastigmine, NOT donepezil, so it is class-level not compound-level evidence for the donepezil PL-vs-OD flip. n=10-12 per protocol, Gottingen lab, M1 MEP readout.
